title: Elastic Reserve Lanes: hybrid reserved + elastic usage pricing and contract playbook
creator: Ava Patel
description: Design and validate a new pricing & contract offering called 'Elastic Reserve Lanes' (ERL): a baseline reserved lane commitment paired with an on-demand elastic overlay and formalized SLA tiers. Goal is to reduce sticker shock for customers who need predictable throughput while offering controlled elasticity for bursts and autoscaling. This ticket captures pricing proposals, contract language templates, enterprise security questionnaire (SQ) checklist, telemetry plan, and an experiment rollout plan.
background: Enterprise customers repeatedly ask for: (1) predictable committed throughput for core traffic, (2) the ability to absorb short bursts without long-term overcommit, and (3) clear SLAs and breach remedies. Current reserved models either force large commits or rely on expensive bursts. ERL aims to provide a predictable baseline (dedicated lanes) priced like reserved capacity plus a metered elastic overlay billed at aggressive incremental rates with built-in guardrails and contractual fallbacks.
hypothesis: If we introduce Elastic Reserve Lanes with a lower effective committed price and a transparent elastic per-GPU-minute overlay, then customers will commit to smaller reserves, adoption of Dedicated will increase by 20% in Q2, and average utilization of reserved capacity will improve (fewer unused hours) without materially increasing peak provisioning costs for Redwood.
proposed_pricing_matrix: Baseline Lanes (committed) - monthly subscription per lane: small (1x V100 class): $6,000/mo, medium (2x V100): $11,000/mo, large (4x A100-like): $20,000/mo.
Elastic Overlay (pay-as-you-go) - per GPU-minute when exceeding baseline: standard elastic: $0.035/GPU-min, priority elastic (higher preemption protection): $0.065/GPU-min.
Burst Credits Option - prepaid burst credits sold in 10k/50k/200k packs with a 12-18% discount vs pay-as-you-go rates.
Autoscale Governance Fee - optional policy & SLO management for high-frequency autoscale: $1,500/mo per customer for advanced policies, included for enterprise tier with 12+ lanes.
Commitment Discounts - 12mo prepay: 10% off baseline lanes; 24mo: 18% off. Volume tiers beyond 100 lanes qualified for bespoke pricing.
Overage Smoothing - customers can opt into a monthly smoothing band (e.g., +/- 15% usage variance) for a fixed premium equal to ~3% of baseline lane cost.
sla_matrix: Silver SLA: 99.5% uptime (regional), latency p95 <= 600ms for small models, monthly credits: 5% of baseline fee for breaches.
Gold SLA: 99.9% uptime (regional + failover), latency p95 <= 350ms for small models, monthly credits: 10% of baseline fee. Requires 6mo commit or 12 lane minimum.

Platinum SLA: 99.95% uptime (multi-region failover), latency p95 <= 200ms for small models, dedicated on-call & response SLAs, credits + engineering remediation clause. Requires legal review and 12-24mo contract.
contract_clauses: Definition: 'Baseline Lanes' = committed GPU capacity assigned to Customer. 'Elastic Overlay' = ephemeral capacity borrowable above baseline and billed per-minute.
Term & Renewal: defaults to auto-renew after committed term unless 60-day notice, with early termination fee equal to 25% of remaining baseline fees for <12mo term.
Capacity Failure Remedies: tiered credits defined in SLA matrix plus optional rollback to previous model variant and emergency autoscale to shared pool.
Data & Security Addenda: customer-managed KMS option for Private deployments, SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 attestations provided on request, with audit scheduling clause.
Preemption/Compatibility: Elastic Overlay workloads are subject to preemption for capacity events; customers may elect Priority Elastic for lower preemption risk (higher price).
enterprise_sq_checklist: KMS: support for CMK (customer-managed keys) in Private deployments and bring-your-own-key with HSM integration.
Logging & Audit: per-request audit logs retained 1yr (configurable), integration with customer SIEM via secure forwarders.
Network Controls: VPC peering, private endpoints, regional egress constraints, and support for on-prem air-gapped package for >24mo contracts.
Identity: SSO (SAML/SCIM), role-based access controls for lane management, token rotation policy documented.
Compliance Evidence: SOC2 Type II report, penetration test summary, vulnerability management cadence (90-day cycles).
Data Residency: options to pin baseline lanes to specific regions for regulatory customers and contractual data residency clause.
Encryption: in-transit TLS1.3 and at-rest AES-256 with optional envelope encryption for sensitive models/keys.
telemetry_metrics: Committed utilization: percent of baseline lane capacity used per 1h window.
Elastic consumption: GPU-minutes consumed via overlay per day and 95th percentile spikes.
Cost per token relative to baseline: rolling 7-day and 30-day aggregates for small/medium models.
SLA signal: regional availability, error budget burn rate, mean time to failover for lane preemption events.
Churn & expansion signals: conversion rate from trial baseline lanes to first paid baseline; average lane growth per customer-month.
rollout_plan: Alpha (internal & pilot customers - 6 customers): validate pricing comprehension, contract negotiation friction, and telemetry accuracy. Target: 6-week pilot starting 2025-03-15.
Beta (invite-only - 25 customers): add automated billing, UI in Console for lane purchase + elastic policy configuration, refine SKU messaging. Target: 2025-05-01.
GA: broad availability with self-serve purchase + sales-assisted negotiation for enterprise. Target: 2025-07-01.
Measurement windows: 30/60/90 day tickets for each cohort with defined success criteria (adoption, usage smoothing, NPS feedback).
decision_log: 2025-02-18 - Decided to separate Priority Elastic (higher price, lower preemption) from standard elastic to address enterprise need for more predictability.
2025-02-25 - Agreed on Smoothing Band optional add-on to reduce billing variance for finance teams; fee set at ~3% baseline cost.
2025-02-28 - Legal flagged early termination fees and asked to add explicit migration assistance clause; product to draft migration support schedule.
open_questions: Should elastic consumption be billed at per-GPU-minute or per-GPU-second granularity for smoother billing? Finance prefers per-minute. Engineering favors per-second for accuracy. Needs tradeoff.
What is the default autoscale policy for baseline vs elastic overlay? Do we enforce safety caps per tenant to avoid runaway billing?
How to present blended unit economics to customers (effective $/token) without exposing Redwood internal margins?
What thresholds should trigger mandatory security review for customers using Priority Elastic?
Does Discounting stack across promo credits and commitment discounts or is there a precedence rule?
